case_title: V. P. Singh Etc. v. The State of Punjab & Ors.
neutral_facts: The accused were teachers and administrators at a college. A student was reprimanded for misconduct in class, which involved an incident with alcohol. The student was suspended and instructed to call his parents as part of disciplinary action. Instead of complying, the student committed suicide by jumping into a canal. Before his death, he sent an SMS to his brother stating his intention to jump into the river and expressing that he did not want to trouble his father. An FIR was registered against the accused for abetment of suicide. The charge sheet included the father's complaint, but there was no independent witness to the incident. The student's apology letter and SMS indicated his personal reasons for the suicide, suggesting he did not blame the accused. The trial court framed charges, but the High Court dismissed the revision petition. The Supreme Court found no evidence of abetment and set aside the charges, acquitting the accused.
